docs.title: SARVe (Scalable Analytics and Research Virtual Environment)
docs.text: SARVe provides computational resources and Jupyter-based interactive environments for scientific computing, data analysis, and research workflows.

docs.title: How to cite the facility in your acknowledgements
docs.text:
Please include the following statement in the acknowledgements section of your presentation, poster, or publication:

The authors acknowledge the computational resources provided by the Scalable Analytics and Research Virtual Environment (SARVe) facility at the School of Theoretical Physics, IPM.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide explains how to set up your working environment on SARVe, create and manage Python environments, and configure JupyterLab kernels for interactive development and analysis.

docs.title: Python environment
docs.text:
We recomment using conda and/or mamba to manage your Python environment.

While you may use the default conda base environment provided by the server, creating your own dedicated environment is generally recommended for reproducibility, package management, and dependency isolation.

Warning

Changes made to the server's default/base environment are not persistent as they are stored in server's ephemeral storage. After your server is stopped or restarted, the base environment will reset to its original state, causing installed packages and modifications to be lost.

Using a dedicated Python environment ensures that your setup remains available across sessions.

Tip

For best performance, it is recommended to work within ~/localstorage directory. See Storage for more details on different storage types and how you could use them in your project.

docs.title: Custom Python environment creation using conda
docs.text:
To quickly create a custom Python environment with conda with name env and using Python 3.13 in localstorage, open a terminal and use: 

conda create --prefix ~/localstorage/env python=3.13
conda init
conda activate ~/localstorage/env

docs.title: Adding a conda environment to Jupyter
docs.text:
The newly created environment is usable in terminal, but not in JupyterLab. To register it in JupyterLab install the ipykernel package inside the environment and use it to create an IPython kernel for the environment.

conda install conda-forge::ipykernel
python -m ipykernel install --user --name env --display-name "Python (env)"

docs.title: Using a custom Python environment in JupyterLab
docs.text:
After creating a Python environment, JupyterLab won't automatically switch to it. To change the environment used by JupyterLab, change it's kernel to the kernel registered for your custom environment:

  1. Open the SARVe JupyterLab interface.
  2. Create a new notebook or open an existing one.

  3. Navigate to: 

    Kernel → Change Kernel

  4. Select:

Python (env)

Your notebook will now use the newly created environment env.

docs.title: Installing a Python package
docs.text:
To install a Python package, use your favorite Python package manager. We recommend using conda or mamba.

Example 
conda install numpy
Note

Python packages are installed in the activated Python environment. Make sure to create and activate a personal environment if you want installed packages to persist over sessions.

docs.title: Installing a system package
docs.text:
The default JupyterLab server runs on ubuntu. To install a system package use apt.

Example 
sudo apt install gcc
Note

System packages are installed in ephemeral storage which means they get reset after your server is stopped. To permanently install a system package you have to create a custom container image and include the package in it. See custom container image creation for details on how the default image is created and how you can add packages to it.

docs.title: Jupyter
docs.text: Jupyter is the main system used in SARVe. JupyterHub is used to spawn user servers. By default it spawns an instance of JupyterLab in your server.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
For each server, there are three types of storage available:

Storage Type Path Description Available across sessions Available across computers Hardware Local storage ~/localstorage Use this for data that need fast access. (e.g. conda environments) NVMe SSD Shared storage ~ Use this for mission critical data. It is slower but lives in a trusted RAID array for maximum safety. RAID Array Ephemeral storage Everywhere else This is the storage assigned to your server for system functions, this gets erased on server shutdown. NVMe SSD

docs.title: Q: Conda activate throws an error and this is the first time using it.
docs.text: A: This probably means that conda is not properly initialized. Use conda init to configures your shell to recognize conda commands. After running this command, restart your terminal or reload your shell configuration.

docs.title: Q: Custom Python environments are not detected in JupyterLab
docs.text:
A: JupyterLab uses IPython and IPython uses kernels to run the Python interpreter. To use a specific Python environment, you have to use that specific installation of Python interpreter. To tell IPython to use another installation of Python interpreter first install ipykernel package in it's environment and then use this command to register it as a IPython kernel:

python -m ipykernel install --user --name test_env --display-name "Python (test_env)"
Info
  • --user → Installs the kernel for your user account.
  • --name test_env → Internal kernel identifier.
  • --display-name "Python (test_env)" → Name displayed in Jupyter.

You can customize the display name if desired.

Then choose the created kernel in JupyterLab by navigating to: 

Kernel → Change Kernel
and selecting the newly created kernel.
